title: Why Lead Sources Dry Up — Four Mechanics Nobody Warns You About
content:
### **Mechanic One — Saturation** 

A channel works partly because few companies are using it. As more arrive, the same homeowner attention is divided among more brands. Nothing about your execution changed. The denominator did. 

###  **Mechanic Two — Homeowner Adaptation** 

People learn to filter. Direct mail worked until homeowners learned to sort it over a recycling bin. Door hangers worked until they became something removed and discarded without reading. The message never gets evaluated, so improving the message does not help. 

###  **Mechanic Three — Platform Economics** 

On paid platforms, cost per lead rises as competition increases, because that is exactly how an auction is designed to behave. A channel can become unprofitable without ever becoming less effective. 

### **Mechanic Four — Seasonal Masking** 

A channel that is already declining can look fine during a busy season, because volume covers it. The decline becomes visible in the slow months, which is the worst possible time to discover it. 

###  **What These Have in Common** 

None of them are execution problems, and none can be fixed by trying harder within the same channel. They are structural, which is why the companies that handle them well are the ones that added a second source before the first one faltered.
